test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 28 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements for a parallel circuit is true?

options.text: The potential difference across individual resistances of a parallel circuit is always unequal.
The net resistance of a parallel circuit is always greater than the sum of individual resistances.
The net resistance of a parallel circuit is always less than the sum of individual resistances.
The net current of a parallel circuit is always less than that of individual currents.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The net resistance of a parallel circuit is always less than the sum of individual resistances.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **parallel circuit, the total (or net) resistance is always less than the smallest individual resistance in the circui**t.
 
• This is **because the current has multiple paths to flow through, which reduces the overall resistance**.
 
• The formula for total resistance Rtotal​ in a parallel circuit is:
 
 
• 1/R total= 1/R1+ 1/R2+ 1/R3
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Difference Between Series and Parallel Circuits**

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Characteristics
 Series Circuit
 Parallel Circuit
 
 

 Definition
 A circuit in which the passage of current is restricted to a single path.
 A circuit that allows current to flow over many paths.
 
 

 Arrangement
 The components are organised in a single line, with the tails of one component attached to the heads of the next.
 The components are arranged so that their heads are aligned and their tails are joined.
 
 

 Pathway of current
 There is just one pathway since the series circuit forms a single loop.
 It creates several loops, allowing current to flow in multiple directions.
 
 

 Current
 The current remains constant.
 In each path, the current is divided in different quantities, depending on the resistance offered by each path.
 
 

 Voltage
 The voltage is split among the components and is determined by their resistance.
 Voltage remains constant.
 
 

 Resistance
 Total resistance increases.
 Total resistance decreases.
 
 

 Capacitance
 Total capacitance decreases.
 Total capacitance increases.
 
 

 Inductance
 Total Inductance increases.
 Total Inductance decreases.
 
 

 Power Supply
 When power supplies are connected in series, the total voltage rises, but the total current stays constant.
 The total voltage remains constant but the total current increases when power supplies are connected in parallel.
